answer: A registry can require each agent key to lock a refundable stake before it may submit bids. The contract binds one stake deposit to one key and slashes it when that key is caught double-claiming a task, so each extra identity ties up scarce capital at risk. A sonnet, shale, and river can label test tasks without affecting the rule. Wealthy attackers can still fund many keys, and slashing depends on reliable evidence of cheating.
